definition_zh: 出血；大出血；大量失血；（人员、资金的）大量流失
definition_en: a heavy or uncontrolled flow of blood from a broken blood vessel, or a rapid damaging loss of people or resources
core_image: 血管裂开一道口子，血连续涌出，纱布一层层被染红
scene: 夜班急诊室的灯还亮着，担架上的伤员小腿伤口不断渗血，血压开始往下掉。The surgeon pressed hard on the wound to stop the hemorrhage.
sceneCN: 这里 hemorrhage 是「大出血」（第 1 个义项：血管破裂后大量失血）；句意为外科医生用力压住伤口，止住了出血。

pos.zh: 大量出血；（人员、资金）急剧流失

derivatives.zh: 由 hemorrhage 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「出血的；出血性的」
同源词，希腊语 haima「血」加 rhein「流」，指肛门静脉肿胀出血形成的痔
由 hemorrhoid 加后缀 -al 构成，义为「痔的；与痔有关的」

senses.title: A heavy flow of blood
senses.definition: a large amount of blood escaping from a ruptured vessel, especially when it cannot be stopped quickly
senses.definitionCN: 血液从破裂血管大量流出，尤其指一时难以止住的情况
senses.example: The patient lost consciousness after a severe hemorrhage.
senses.exampleCN: 病人大出血之后失去了意识。
senses.why: Greek haima means blood and rhegnynai means to burst, so the word pictures blood bursting out of a vessel rather than merely leaking.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 haima 意为「血」，rhegnynai 意为「破裂」，所以这个词的画面是血从血管破口涌出，而不只是慢慢渗出。

senses.title: Bleeding hidden inside the body
senses.definition: bleeding that happens inside a body cavity or organ, where no blood is visible from outside the body
senses.definitionCN: 发生在体腔或器官内部的出血，血液不从体表流出
senses.example: A fall from the ladder caused an internal hemorrhage in his abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，造成了腹部内出血。
senses.why: The same bursting image is turned inward: the vessel breaks, but the skin stays closed, so the blood collects in a space no one can see.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「破裂」的画面转向体内：血管破了，皮肤却没有开口，血于是积在看不见的地方。

senses.title: A single bleeding episode
senses.definition: one countable episode of heavy bleeding, as noted in a medical record or a diagnosis
senses.definitionCN: 可计数的一次大量出血事件，常见于病历或诊断记录
senses.example: The chart lists three hemorrhages since the patient was admitted.
senses.exampleCN: 病历上记录着病人入院以来发生的三次出血。
senses.why: Doctors count these events, so the mass noun also becomes a count noun: each burst of bleeding is one hemorrhage.
senses.whyCN: 医生要把这类事件计数，于是这个不可数名词也可作可数名词：每一次出血就是一次 hemorrhage。

senses.title: To bleed heavily
senses.definition: to lose blood heavily from a broken vessel
senses.definitionCN: 因血管破裂而大量失血
senses.example: The wound began to hemorrhage before the ambulance arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 救护车赶到之前，伤口已经开始大量出血。
senses.why: The verb turns the burst into an event in time: the vessel opens and the blood keeps coming.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「破裂」变成时间中的事件：血管一开，血就不断涌出。

senses.title: A rapid loss of people or resources
senses.definition: a rapid and damaging loss of staff, money, customers, or other resources
senses.definitionCN: 人员、资金、客户等资源迅速而有害的流失
senses.example: The department suffered a hemorrhage of experienced nurses after the shift system changed.
senses.exampleCN: 排班制度改变之后，这个科室经历了资深护士的大量流失。
senses.why: Blood is what keeps a body alive; when skilled staff or money leave an organization, the image of life draining away fits exactly.
senses.whyCN: 血维持身体存活；当熟练人员或资金离开一个组织时，「生命在流失」的画面正好合用。

senses.title: To lose something rapidly
senses.definition: to lose money, staff, or support rapidly and in damaging amounts
senses.definitionCN: 资金、人员或支持以有害的数量迅速流失
senses.example: The clinic hemorrhaged cash during the months it stayed open without patients.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在那几个月没有病人的情况下持续开诊，资金急剧流失。
senses.why: Once the noun can name any vital resource, the verb can describe the organization itself losing that resource.
senses.whyCN: 一旦名词可以指任何维系组织的资源，动词就能描述组织本身正在失去这种资源。

intro.en: Hemorrhage goes back through Latin medical writing to two Greek words, one for blood and one for bursting.
intro.cn: hemorrhage 经由拉丁语医学文献上溯到两个希腊词，一个表示「血」，一个表示「破裂」。

items.en: Haima is the Greek noun for blood, and it survives in many medical combining forms.
items.cn: haima 是希腊语中表示「血」的名词，至今留在许多医学构词成分之中。

items.en: Rhegnynai means to break or burst, and it supplies the second half of the compound.
items.cn: rhegnynai 意为「破裂、爆开」，提供这个复合词的后半部分。

items.en: The Greeks joined the two into haimorrhagia, a bursting forth of blood, a term already used in medical writing.
items.cn: 希腊人把两者合成 haimorrhagia，意为「血的迸流」，这一术语在希腊医学文献中已有使用。

items.en: Medical Latin borrowed the Greek term as haemorrhagia and kept the ae spelling.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语借入这个希腊术语，写作 haemorrhagia，保留了 ae 拼法。

items.en: English takes the word from Latin in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, at first as a learned medical noun.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪从拉丁语引入该词，最初是学术性的医学名词。

items.en: American usage simplifies ae to e and writes hemorrhage, while British English keeps haemorrhage.
items.cn: 美式用法把 ae 简化为 e，写作 hemorrhage，英式英语则保留 haemorrhage。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same Greek blood root or on the same spelling; the near-meaning group holds ordinary bleeding words with a wider or narrower reach.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊「血」词根构成的词以及同一词的拼写变体；近义组收普通的「出血」说法，范围有宽有窄。

entries.definition: An adjective describing something that relates to, or is caused by, heavy bleeding.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「出血的、出血性的」，指与大量出血有关或由其引起的。

entries.definition: A swollen vein in the lower rectum, named from the Greek words for blood and flowing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「痔」，由希腊语「血」与「流」组合得名，与 hemorrhage 同源。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same word, keeping the ae that American English drops.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的英式拼法，保留美式英语省略掉的 ae；只是拼写不同，并非另一个词。

entries.definition: The general word for blood coming out of the body, milder and less technical than hemorrhage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「出血」，是最一般的说法，语气比 hemorrhage 轻，也更不专业。

entries.definition: The amount of blood a patient has lost, used in clinical measurement rather than as a name for the event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失血、失血量」，多用于临床计量，而不是给出血事件命名。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for losing blood, which may be slight and need not be dramatic.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「流血、出血」，可以是轻微的，不必像 hemorrhage 那样严重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real Greek root and on the clinical phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依靠真实的希腊词根，以及这个词实际出现的临床搭配。

normal.en: Haima is blood and rhegnynai is to burst: a hemorrhage is blood bursting out, not just a small cut.
normal.cn: haima 是「血」，rhegnynai 是「破裂」：hemorrhage 是血破管而出，而不只是一个小伤口。

normal.en: The -rrhagia part of related medical terms always signals a flow or discharge, often of blood.
normal.cn: 相关医学术语中的 -rrhagia 部分总表示「流、涌出」，多半指血。

normal.en: Severe hemorrhage, internal hemorrhage and postpartum hemorrhage are the phrases to know first.
normal.cn: severe hemorrhage、internal hemorrhage 与 postpartum hemorrhage 是最该先记住的三个搭配。

normal.en: British writing keeps haemorrhage, while American writing drops the a to make hemorrhage.
normal.cn: 英式写作保留 haemorrhage，美式写作去掉 a，写成 hemorrhage。

normal.en: A hemorrhage of nurses or of cash uses the same image: something vital is draining away fast.
normal.cn: a hemorrhage of nurses 或 a hemorrhage of cash 用的是同一个画面：维持生命的东西正在迅速流走。

abstract.en: See a pipe under pressure split open and red water spray across a white floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一根受压的水管裂开，红色的水喷溅在白色地面上。

abstract.en: Now the same pipe splits behind a closed wall, and the water only rises silently inside the room.
abstract.cn: 再想象同一根管子在封闭的墙后裂开，水只在墙内悄悄上涨。

abstract.en: A nurse counts each split on a chart, one line for one burst, because each event must be recorded.
abstract.cn: 护士在表格上记下每一次裂口，一次迸裂画一道线，因为每次发作都要记录。

examples.en: The surgeon worked quickly to control the hemorrhage from the femoral artery.
examples.cn: 外科医生迅速操作，控制住了股动脉的出血。

examples.en: After the crash, scans showed a small internal hemorrhage near his liver.
examples.cn: 事故之后，扫描显示他肝脏附近有一处小的内出血。

examples.en: The hospital hemorrhaged money for two years before the new ward opened.
examples.cn: 在新病区启用之前，这家医院连续两年资金大量流失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑魔瑞吉」——黑魔（hemo）一挥手，血管破裂、血涌出来，记作「大出血」；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 希腊语 haima「血」加 rhegnynai「破裂」，合成 haimorrhagia「血的迸流」，再经拉丁语 haemorrhagia 进入英语；核心义是「血管破裂、血大量涌出」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses apply one bursting image: visible bleeding, hidden internal bleeding, a counted episode, the act of bleeding, and the figurative draining of people or money.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项共用同一个「破裂涌出」的画面：看得见的大出血、藏在体内的内出血、可计数的一次发作、出血这个动作，以及人员或资金被抽干的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vessel splits and blood pours out faster than the body can replace it.
core.cn: 核心意象：血管裂开，血涌出的速度快过身体补充的速度。

branches.en: THE WOUND: blood leaves a broken vessel where everyone can see it.
branches.cn: 伤口线：血从破裂的血管流出，人人都看得见。

branches.en: THE CAVITY: the same break happens inside, and the blood collects out of sight.
branches.cn: 体腔线：同样的破裂发生在体内，血积在看不见的地方。

branches.en: THE RECORD: each burst is counted as one event in the chart.
branches.cn: 病历线：每一次迸裂在病历上记作一次发作。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the body doing what the noun describes.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指身体正在做名词所描述的事。

branches.en: THE ORGANIZATION: staff and money can drain away like blood, and the verb carries that loss.
branches.cn: 组织线：人员和资金可以像血一样流走，动词承担这层流失义。

intro.en: Hemorrhage is a Greek compound imported through Latin; English adds only the adjective ending -ic and a related noun in hemorrhoid.
intro.cn: hemorrhage 是经拉丁语传入的希腊语复合词；英语只再加上形容词词尾 -ic，另有一个同源名词 hemorrhoid。

latinIntro.en: The two Greek roots are haima, blood, and rhegnynai, to burst; medical Latin recorded the compound as haemorrhagia before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 两个希腊词根是 haima「血」与 rhegnynai「破裂」；医学拉丁语把复合词记作 haemorrhagia，之后英语才借入。

items.example: Haima supplies the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: haima 提供这个复合词的前一半。

items.example: Rhegnynai supplies the idea of something bursting.
items.exampleCN: rhegnynai 提供「某物爆裂」的意象。

items.example: The suffix appears in haimorrhagia and other medical terms.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾出现在 haimorrhagia 以及其他医学术语中。

items.example: Greek medical writers used the compound for heavy bleeding.
items.exampleCN: 希腊医学作者用这个复合词表示大量出血。

items.example: Medical Latin kept the Greek ae spelling.
items.exampleCN: 医学拉丁语保留了希腊语的 ae 拼法。

items.example: Hemo- opens many clinical words, such as hemoglobin.
items.exampleCN: hemo- 开头的临床词很多，例如 hemoglobin。

items.example: English borrowed the noun through medical Latin.
items.exampleCN: 英语经医学拉丁语借入这个名词。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把这个名词变成形容词。

items.example: It forms hemorrhagic from hemorrhage.
items.exampleCN: 它由 hemorrhage 构成 hemorrhagic。

definition_zh: 肾；肾脏；（供食用的）动物腰子
definition_en: one of the two organs in the lower back that filter waste from the blood and make urine
core_image: 后腰内侧一对蚕豆形的滤器，血液从中流过，废物被滤下、变成尿
scene: 查房时，医生在病历上圈出腰部的位置，告诉家属检查结果不太乐观。One of his kidneys had stopped filtering waste properly.
sceneCN: 这里 kidney 是「肾脏」（第 1 个义项：过滤血液、生成尿液的器官）；句意为他的一个肾脏已经不能正常过滤废物了。

derivatives.zh: 由 kidney 与 bean 复合而成，因豆子形状像肾，义为「芸豆；腰豆」
由 kidney 与 stone 复合而成，义为「肾结石」
由 kidney 加 -shaped 构成，义为「肾形的；豆形的」

senses.title: The organ that filters the blood
senses.definition: one of the two bean-shaped organs in the lower back that remove waste from the blood and produce urine
senses.definitionCN: 位于后腰、呈蚕豆形的一对器官，负责清除血液中的废物并生成尿液
senses.example: Each kidney contains about a million tiny filters called nephrons.
senses.exampleCN: 每个肾脏约含一百万个叫做肾单位的微小滤器。
senses.why: The word names the organ itself, the physical filter that the other senses describe or borrow from.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指器官本身，也就是其余义项所描述或借用的那个实体滤器。

senses.title: Renal function shown by tests
senses.definition: the working capacity of the kidneys, as shown by blood and urine tests or by the amount of urine produced
senses.definitionCN: 肾脏的工作能力，由血液与尿液检查或尿量反映出来
senses.example: Her kidneys are still strong enough to clear the contrast dye.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肾功能仍然足以排出造影剂。
senses.why: Because the organ is judged by what it does, doctors say the kidneys are failing, naming the function by the organ.
senses.whyCN: 正因为器官是按其功能来评判的，医生会说肾在衰竭，用器官名代替了功能。

senses.title: An animal kidney eaten as food
senses.definition: the kidney of cattle, sheep, or pigs, cooked and eaten as meat or used in pies and stews
senses.definitionCN: 牛、羊或猪的肾脏，煮熟后作为肉类食用，或用于馅饼与炖菜
senses.example: The butcher trimmed the lamb kidneys and put them beside the chops.
senses.exampleCN: 肉贩修整好羊腰子，放在羊排旁边。
senses.why: The organ keeps its shape and name on the plate: what filtered blood in the animal is sold as offal in the shop.
senses.whyCN: 器官上了餐桌仍保留原来的形状与名称：在动物体内过滤血液的东西，在店里作为内脏出售。

senses.title: The same kind or temperament
senses.definition: in the phrase of the same kidney, of the same kind, type, or temperament, often used of people
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「of the same kidney」，指同一种类、类型或气质，多用来形容人
senses.example: The two surgeons were of the same kidney: blunt, tireless, and impatient with ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位外科医生是同一类人：直率、不知疲倦，也讨厌繁文缛节。
senses.why: Old medicine held that organs shaped temperament, so kidney came to mean the kind of person one is; the phrase survives as a formal idiom.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的医学认为器官决定性情，于是 kidney 引申为人的类型；这个短语作为正式习语保留了下来。

senses.title: A bean-like outline
senses.definition: a curved bean-like outline, as in kidney bean or a kidney-shaped table, named after the organ
senses.definitionCN: 像蚕豆一样的弧形轮廓，如 kidney bean 或肾形桌，都因形似肾脏而得名
senses.example: The pool has a kidney shape, with two rounded lobes and a narrow waist.
senses.exampleCN: 这个泳池呈肾形，有两个圆润的叶和一个窄腰。
senses.why: Because the organ has a distinctive curved outline, its name became a shape word for beans, pools, and tables.
senses.whyCN: 因为器官有独特的弧形轮廓，它的名字就成了豆子、泳池和桌子的形状词。

intro.en: Kidney is a Middle English word of uncertain origin, first recorded as kidnere, and the earliest parts are still debated.
intro.cn: kidney 是一个来源不确定的中古英语词，最早记作 kidnere，其构成成分至今仍有争议。

items.en: The second element is generally connected with Old Norse nyra, kidney, which also gives German Niere and Dutch nier.
items.cn: 一般认为后半部分与古诺尔斯语 nyra「肾」有关，这个词还给出德语 Niere 与荷兰语 nier。

items.en: The word first appears in Middle English as kidnere, with the second element already in place and the first unclear.
items.cn: 这个词最早以中古英语 kidnere 出现，后半部分已经成形，前半部分仍不清楚。

items.en: Spelling variants such as kideney and kidney compete, and the modern spelling is fixed only later.
items.cn: kideney、kidney 等拼写变体并存，现代拼写是后来才固定下来的。

items.en: The old belief that the organ governed temperament produces the phrase of the same kidney.
items.cn: 旧时认为肾脏决定性情的看法，产生了「of the same kidney」这一短语。

items.en: Modern English adds the food sense and a large family of compounds such as kidney bean and kidney stone.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了食用义，以及 kidney bean、kidney stone 等一大批复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds compounds built on kidney; the near-meaning group holds the medical words for the same organ and its diseases, which come from other roots.
note.cn: 形近组收由 kidney 构成的复合词；近义组收指同一器官及其疾病的医学词，它们来自别的词根。

entries.definition: A bean with a curved shape like a kidney, cooked and eaten as a vegetable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「芸豆、腰豆」，因豆子形似肾脏而得名，常作蔬菜食用。

entries.definition: An adjective for an object with the curved outline of a kidney.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肾形的、豆形的」，指物体具有肾脏那样的弧形轮廓。

entries.definition: A hard mass of salts that forms inside a kidney and can block the flow of urine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肾结石」，是肾脏内形成的坚硬盐类团块，可阻塞尿液流通。

entries.definition: The medical adjective meaning relating to the kidneys; it comes from Latin ren, a different root from kidney.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肾的」，是医学专用说法；它来自拉丁语 ren，与 kidney 的词根不同，只是同指一个器官。

entries.definition: The tiny filtering unit inside a kidney, named from the Greek word for kidney.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肾单位」，是肾脏内部微小的过滤单元，名称来自希腊语的「肾」。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the kidney, a clinical condition rather than the organ itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肾炎」，指肾脏的炎症，是临床病症而不是器官本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Middle English form, the common compounds, and the medical words that surround kidney.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的中古英语形式、常见复合词，以及围绕 kidney 的医学词。

normal.en: The Middle English form is kidnere, and the modern word has shortened and respelled it.
normal.cn: 中古英语形式是 kidnere，现代词只是把它缩短并改写了拼写。

normal.en: Kidney bean, kidney stone and kidney-shaped all keep the organ image in front of the noun.
normal.cn: kidney bean、kidney stone 与 kidney-shaped 都把器官的形象放在词的前面。

normal.en: German Niere and Dutch nier are cousins of the second half of kidney.
normal.cn: 德语 Niere 与荷兰语 nier 是 kidney 后半部分的同族词。

normal.en: Of the same kidney means of the same kind, an idiom older than modern medicine.
normal.cn: 「of the same kidney」意为同一类，这个习语比现代医学更古老。

normal.en: Renal is the medical adjective, but it comes from Latin ren, not from kidney.
normal.cn: renal 是医学形容词，但它来自拉丁语 ren，而不是来自 kidney。

abstract.en: See two bean-shaped filters against the back wall, blood flowing in and clean urine flowing out.
abstract.cn: 想象后腰内侧两枚蚕豆形的滤器，血液流进去，清亮的尿液流出来。

abstract.en: See a gauge on the clinic wall drop as the filters slow down, and the nurse writes the number on a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象诊室墙上的仪表随着滤器变慢而下降，护士把数字记在表格上。

abstract.en: See the same bean shape on a butcher block, trimmed and ready for the pan.
abstract.cn: 再想象同样的豆形出现在砧板上，修整干净，等着下锅。

examples.en: The scan showed a small stone lodged in his left kidney.
examples.cn: 扫描显示他左肾里卡着一颗小结石。

examples.en: Doctors watched her kidney function drop after the infection.
examples.cn: 感染之后，医生持续观察她的肾功能下降。

examples.en: She soaked the kidney beans overnight before cooking them.
examples.cn: 她把芸豆泡了一夜才下锅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奇的你」——小孩（kid）指着自己的腰侧说，这里藏着两颗豆子形的滤器；只是谐音联想，与中古英语 kidnere 无关。

root: 中古英语 kidnere（来源不确定，一般认为后半与古诺尔斯语 nyra「肾」有关）→ kidney；核心义是「后腰内侧那对蚕豆形的滤器」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses start from the organ: its filtering work, its meat, its use in an old idiom about temperament, and its bean-like shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都从器官出发：它的过滤功能、可食用的腰子、旧习语中代表性情的用法，以及蚕豆般的外形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bean-shaped filters against the back wall, taking waste out of the blood.
core.cn: 核心意象：后腰内侧一对蚕豆形滤器，把废物从血液里取出来。

branches.en: THE ORGAN: the bean-shaped body that does the filtering.
branches.cn: 器官线：那颗蚕豆形、真正执行过滤的实体。

branches.en: THE TEST: what the organ does is measured and reported as kidney function.
branches.cn: 检查线：器官所做的事被测量并报告为肾功能。

branches.en: THE PLATE: the same organ appears as food under the same name.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：同一个器官以同样的名字出现在食物里。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: an old belief about organs and character leaves one formal idiom.
branches.cn: 性情线：旧时关于器官与性格的看法留下了一个正式习语。

branches.en: THE OUTLINE: the curved silhouette becomes a shape word for beans and pools.
branches.cn: 轮廓线：那道弧形轮廓成了豆子和泳池的形状词。

intro.en: Kidney is a Middle English word rather than a Latin one; English built its compounds and kept a separate Latin-rooted medical adjective, renal.
intro.cn: kidney 是中古英语词，并非拉丁语词；英语为它造了复合词，医学上另用拉丁词根的形容词 renal。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word shares the root of kidney; Latin names the organ with ren, which gives the medical adjective renal, so no Latin cognate is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词与 kidney 同根；拉丁语用 ren 称呼这个器官，并由此产生医学形容词 renal，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The second element is generally traced to this word.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分一般认为可以追溯到这个词。

items.example: Kidnere is the form that opens the English record.
items.exampleCN: kidnere 是英语记录中最早的形式。

items.example: Kideney appears beside kidney in Middle English texts.
items.exampleCN: 在中古英语文本里，kideney 与 kidney 并见。

items.example: Kidney is the settled modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: kidney 是固定下来的现代拼写。

items.example: The plural is used when both organs are meant.
items.exampleCN: 指两侧器官时用复数。

items.meaning: a bean shaped like a kidney
items.example: The compound names the bean by its shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词按形状给豆子命名。

items.meaning: a hard mass formed in the kidney
items.example: The compound names a common kidney disorder.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名一种常见的肾脏疾病。

items.meaning: having the curved outline of a kidney
items.example: The compound describes an outline, not an organ.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词描述轮廓，而不是器官。

items.example: The suffix forms kidney-shaped.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 kidney-shaped。

items.example: Renal supplies the clinical adjective that kidney lacks.
items.exampleCN: renal 提供了 kidney 所缺的临床形容词。

definition_zh: 肠；肠道；（古）内部的；国内的
definition_en: the long tube that runs from the stomach to the anus, where food is digested and nutrients are absorbed
core_image: 腹腔里盘绕数圈的长管，食物在其中被慢慢拆解、吸收，残渣被推向出口
scene: 手术室的无影灯下，医生顺着腹部切口找到那段盘绕的管道，准备切掉坏死的部分。The surgeon removed the blocked part of the small intestine and reconnected the two ends.
sceneCN: 这里 intestine 是「肠、肠道」（第 1 个义项：消化道的管状部分）；句意为外科医生切除了小肠梗阻的一段，再把两端接起来。

pos.zh: 内部的；国内的（古义，多用于书面）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「肠的；肠道的」
由 intestinal 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「经肠道地」
由 gastro-「胃」与 intestinal「肠的」复合而成，义为「胃肠的」

senses.title: The tube of the lower digestive tract
senses.definition: the long coiled tube that continues from the stomach and ends at the anus, where digestion finishes and waste is formed
senses.definitionCN: 从胃延伸、盘绕腹腔并止于肛门的管道，消化在此完成，粪便在此形成
senses.example: Food may spend more than twenty hours passing through the intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 食物经过肠道可能需要二十多个小时。
senses.why: Latin intestinum simply named the inner tube, the space inside the body through which food travels.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intestinum 直接命名了体内那根「里面的管子」，食物正是从这条内部通道经过。

senses.title: The small intestine, where nutrients are absorbed
senses.definition: the upper, narrower section of the intestine, about six metres long, where most nutrients are absorbed
senses.definitionCN: 肠道较窄的上段，长约六米，大部分营养物质在此被吸收
senses.example: Most of the iron in a meal is absorbed in the small intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 一餐中的大部分铁在小肠里被吸收。
senses.why: English splits the tube by width: the narrower upper stretch is the small intestine, and the name records its diameter rather than its length.
senses.whyCN: 英语按粗细把这条管子分成两段：较窄的上段就是 small intestine，名字记的是直径而不是长度。

senses.title: The large intestine, where water is absorbed
senses.definition: the wider, shorter lower section of the intestine, which absorbs water and salts and compacts waste into stool
senses.definitionCN: 肠道较宽较短的下段，吸收水分与盐分，并把废物压成粪便
senses.example: The large intestine reclaims water that would otherwise be lost.
senses.exampleCN: 大肠把本来会流失的水分回收回来。
senses.why: The same naming logic gives the wide lower stretch; it is large in width, not in length.
senses.whyCN: 同样的命名逻辑给出较宽的下段：它「大」在宽度，而不在长度。

senses.title: Animal intestine used as a casing
senses.definition: the cleaned intestine of an animal, used to hold sausage meat or as a natural casing in cooking
senses.definitionCN: 清洗过的动物肠子，用来装香肠肉馅，或在烹饪中作为天然肠衣
senses.example: The sausages are filled into natural intestine rather than plastic casing.
senses.exampleCN: 这些香肠灌进天然肠衣，而不是塑料肠衣。
senses.why: The organ is tough, elastic, and hollow, so butchers kept using it as a container long after it stopped being an organ.
senses.whyCN: 这个器官坚韧、有弹性、又是空心的，所以屠户在它不再是器官之后，仍长期把它当容器使用。

senses.title: Internal or domestic, in older formal use
senses.definition: internal, civil, or domestic, describing conflict or matters inside a country, in older formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 内部的、国内的，用于描述一国之内的冲突或事务，属较古的正式用法
senses.example: The history book describes a long intestine war between the northern and southern provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这本史书描述了南北两省之间一场漫长的内战。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the literal Latin meaning, inside, and applies it to a country rather than a body.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了拉丁语「在里面」的本义，只是把「内部」从身体移用到国家。

intro.en: Intestine comes straight from Latin intestinum, the inner tube, built on intus, within.
intro.cn: intestine 直接来自拉丁语 intestinum「里面的管子」，由 intus「在内」构成。

items.en: Intus is an adverb meaning within or inside, and it is the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: intus 是副词，意为「在内、在内部」，是整个词族的种子。

items.en: The adjective intestinus means internal or inward, describing what lies inside a thing.
items.cn: 形容词 intestinus 意为「内部的、里面的」，描述处在某物内部的东西。

items.en: The neuter noun intestinum names the inner tube itself, and the plural intestina names the guts.
items.cn: 中性名词 intestinum 直接命名这根「内部的管子」，复数 intestina 指整副肠子。

items.en: Old French intestin carries the word into medieval French with the same anatomical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 intestin 把这个词带入中世纪法语，解剖学含义不变。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century, at first mostly in medical and learned writing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，最初多用于医学与学术写作。

items.en: Modern usage prefers the plural intestines for the organs, while the singular survives in compounds and in the old adjective sense.
items.cn: 现代用法多以复数 intestines 指整副肠子，单数则留在复合词与古老的形容词义之中。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the Latin root; the near-meaning group holds the everyday and clinical names for the same stretch of gut.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根构成的词；近义组收指同一段消化管的日常说法与临床名称。

entries.definition: The adjective for anything relating to the intestine.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肠的、肠道的」，指与肠有关的。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning by or through the intestine, used in medical descriptions.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「经肠道地」，多用于医学描述。

entries.definition: The compound adjective for the stomach and intestines taken together.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「胃肠的」，由 gastro-「胃」与 intestinal 复合而成。

entries.definition: The everyday and medical word for the intestine, usually used in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肠」，日常与医学都用，通常作复数，与 intestine 所指相同。

entries.definition: An informal or anatomical word for the whole digestive tube, also used of courage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肠子、消化道」，语气较口语，也可指勇气。

entries.definition: The longest part of the large intestine, a narrower clinical term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结肠」，是大肠最长的一段，范围比 intestine 窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the width-based compounds, and the medical family around intestine.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根、按粗细构成的复合词，以及围绕 intestine 的医学词族。

normal.en: Intus means within: the intestine is literally the tube inside the body.
normal.cn: intus 意为「在内」：intestine 字面上就是身体里面的那根管子。

normal.en: Intestinal, intestinally and gastrointestinal all keep the Latin root visible.
normal.cn: intestinal、intestinally 与 gastrointestinal 都让拉丁词根清晰可见。

normal.en: Small intestine and large intestine name width, not length, which is why the small one is longer.
normal.cn: small intestine 与 large intestine 命名的是粗细而不是长短，所以「小」的那段反而更长。

normal.en: The plural intestines is the usual form when the whole set of organs is meant.
normal.cn: 指整副器官时，通常用复数 intestines。

normal.en: The old adjective sense, internal, survives in formal phrases such as intestine war.
normal.cn: 「内部的」这个古老形容词义留在 intestine war 这类正式短语里。

abstract.en: See a long folded tube coiled like a garden hose inside the belly, food sliding along it.
abstract.cn: 想象腹腔里一根像花园水管那样盘绕折叠的长管，食物顺着它滑行。

abstract.en: See the upper narrow half of the hose with tiny fingers reaching into it and pulling nutrients out.
abstract.cn: 想象水管较窄的上半段伸出细小的指状绒毛，把养分拉出来。

abstract.en: See the lower wider half pressing the leftover paste dry and pushing it toward the exit.
abstract.cn: 再想象较宽的下半段把剩下的糊状物压干，推向出口。

examples.en: The camera passed through his stomach and into the intestine without finding a bleed.
examples.cn: 胶囊内镜从他的胃进入肠道，没有发现出血点。

examples.en: A blockage in the small intestine can cause severe vomiting and pain.
examples.cn: 小肠梗阻可以引起剧烈呕吐和疼痛。

examples.en: The large intestine absorbs water before waste leaves the body.
examples.cn: 大肠在废物排出体外之前吸收水分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特斯汀」——记住 in 就是「在里面」，身体里面那条盘绕的长管就是肠道；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 intus「在内」→ intestinus「内部的」→ intestinum「里面的管子、肠」→ 古法语 intestin → 英语 intestine；核心义是「身体内部那根盘绕的消化管」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow the inner tube outward: the whole tract, its narrow upper half, its wide lower half, its use as a casing, and the old adjective meaning internal.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项沿着这根「内部的管子」展开：整条肠道、较窄的上段、较宽的下段、作为肠衣的用途，以及「内部的」这个古老形容词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long tube coiled inside the belly, with food moving slowly along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：腹腔里一根盘绕的长管，食物沿着它慢慢前行。

branches.en: THE TRACT: one long inner tube from stomach to anus.
branches.cn: 整条线：从胃到肛门的一根内部长管。

branches.en: THE UPPER HALF: the narrow stretch where nutrients are taken in.
branches.cn: 上段线：较窄的一段，养分在这里被吸收。

branches.en: THE LOWER HALF: the wide stretch where water is taken back.
branches.cn: 下段线：较宽的一段，水分在这里被回收。

branches.en: THE CASING: the hollow tube reused as a container for meat.
branches.cn: 肠衣线：这根空心的管子被改用作装肉的容器。

branches.en: THE INSIDE: the adjective keeps the plain Latin sense of internal.
branches.cn: 内部线：形容词保留拉丁语「内部」的本义。

intro.en: Intestine is a Latin word taken into English through French; English builds its adjectives with -al and -ly and joins it to gastro-.
intro.cn: intestine 是经法语进入英语的拉丁词；英语用 -al 与 -ly 构成形容词和副词，并让它与 gastro- 组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin intus, intestinus and intestinum are all recorded, so the family needs no reconstructed form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intus、intestinus 与 intestinum 均有文献记录，这个词族不需要重构形式。

items.example: Intus is the base of the adjective and the noun.
items.exampleCN: intus 是形容词与名词的基础。

items.example: The adjective describes what lies inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述处在内部的东西。

items.example: The noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The plural names the whole set of organs.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式指整副器官。

items.example: Old French carries the Latin noun onward.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把拉丁名词继续传下去。

items.example: English borrows the noun in the fourteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十四世纪借入这个名词。

items.meaning: the organs taken as a set
items.example: The plural is the usual form for the organs.
items.exampleCN: 指整副器官时通常用复数。

items.example: The suffix -al forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成这个形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成这个副词。

items.example: It forms intestinal from intestine.
items.exampleCN: 它由 intestine 构成 intestinal。

items.example: Gastro- joins intestinal to make gastrointestinal.
items.exampleCN: gastro- 与 intestinal 组合成 gastrointestinal。
